title: A periodic counterexample to the diffuse allocation characterization
verdict: PASS for deterministic pointwise-covariant preserving allocations of the original observed state.

actual.support: Original finite checker and exact certificate inspected and replayed.

proof: The phase orbit is observed and Borel because the parametrization is continuous and injective from a compact space. Pointwise covariance reduces maps to a pure translation on each periodic line family. Unit horizontal segments give exact atomic measure equality per period. Unequal masses exclude both swapping and collisions, even for noninjective maps.
The mass sample from a shifted half-open unit square moves the root to a heavy line with probability 2/3. The heavy-root event has probability 0 initially, so the first marginal already fails.

A deterministic covariant lift over a Lebesgue coordinate translates that coordinate by a base-dependent amount. Tonelli on rectangles gives preservation equivalence; restricting a product to a unit strip recovers the base measure measurably. Last–Thorisson’s 2009 atomic example and 2014/15 product equivalence give the full historical conclusion.
A genuinely random preserving kernel does move the light root to a heavy line. The periodic example has a continuous stabilizer and is singular.
primary: Thorisson’s Problem 4.1 checked by the independent reviewer. Root browser fetch of the current URL timed out, and root confirmed the original formal Problem 7.5.

independent.result: PASS; static 204 members/203 manifest items/frozen 26, plus 144 exact residue and 755 interval tests.

scope: Singular, diffuse measure with continuous translation stabilizer. No extension to positive-density, free-action, one-dimensional, randomized-kernel or independent-background variants. The full negative consequence is attributed to the classical inputs and elementary transfer. No follow-up cleared the bar.
